subject.title: fix(gateway): restrict backend self-pairing shared auth

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally remove shared token/password auth from the local backend self-pairing scope-preservation exception now?
rationale: The patch is a narrow hardening for a live Gateway auth boundary, but it intentionally breaks documented shipped behavior for any backend client relying on shared token/password scope preservation.

options.title: Accept the hardened boundary
options.body: Resolve conflicts against current main and merge the fail-closed behavior with security-owner acceptance of the compatibility break.

options.title: Add a transition path
options.body: If shipped backend callers depend on this behavior, add a tested warning, migration, or compatibility window before removing shared-token/password scope preservation.

options.title: Pause for broader auth design
options.body: If maintainers want to revisit the full trusted-loopback operator model, pause this PR and track a broader Gateway auth design decision instead.

recommendation.title: Accept the hardened boundary
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts against current main and merge the fail-closed behavior with security-owner acceptance of the compatibility break.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS assigns the touched Gateway auth and Gateway security docs surfaces to this owner group, and the unresolved question is a security boundary decision.
